title: Former soccer agent Jonathan Barnett denies ‘sex slave’ accusations as ‘ridiculous’
content:
Jonathan Barnett, the former high-profile soccer agent, has denied any wrongdoing after being accused of “threatening to kill” a woman who alleges he raped and tortured her if she spoke out.

Barnett has also rejected the allegation from the woman, an Australian known as Jane Doe to protect her identity, that he instructed her to search for “slaves” in California in September 2018.

Doe’s statement, in a U.S. court filing dated January 23, alleges that Barnett “forced me to work in servitude to him, controlling me using numerous means, including psychological and physical abuse, threats to harm me and my children, and tricking me into financial dependence”.

The allegations made against Barnett cover a six-year period between July 2017 and November 2023.

“Barnett exerted control over my life as his sex slave, forcing me to follow a rigid set of rules, engage in commercial sex acts, and regularly commit self-harm and perform other dehumanizing acts,” Doe’s statement in January said.

However, Barnett has denied all her claims, including her allegation that he “lured” her to London in 2017, and described her claims that their relationship was “not consensual” nor “personal” as “false”.

“Plaintiff’s allegation that I threatened the lives of Plaintiff and her children is false and absurd, and, again, the accusation has no relevance to the Court’s determination of personal jurisdiction,” Barnett’s response, filed on February 9, said.

“The allegation at paragraph 7 of Plaintiff’s declaration that I somehow exercised coercive control over Plaintiff until she ‘escaped’ in November 2023 is ridiculous and denied.

“To the contrary, up until her ‘escape’ in November 2023, Plaintiff freely and frequently travelled throughout the world, including trips to Australia, South Korea, Canada and Thailand, as well as the purported trip to California in September 2018.

“Plaintiff’s suggestion that she was controlled by me and unable to leave the relationship is preposterous. Plaintiff could have voluntarily terminated our relationship at any point.”

Barnett also said Doe had “no difficulty terminating the relationship after I refused to pay her the additional amounts she demanded from me”.

The 76-year-old responded to the alleged victim’s claim that he has maintained a “library of videos and photographs” of Doe “engaging in humiliating acts and self-harm” as “absolutely false”.

“Plaintiff offers no proof in support of her accusation, and it is apparent that it was included in her declaration merely to prejudice the Court against me,” Barnett added.

Barnett has previously claimed that he paid Doe “well in excess of £1,000,000 in London” following the end of their relationship, because she “she threatened to publicly disclose the relationship unless I paid her significant sums of money”.

Barnett, who was once one of the highest-profile agents in football before retiring in 2023, founded the Stellar Group before it was purchased by ICM Partners and later taken over by CAA.

He helped broker Gareth Bale’s then world-record transfer from Tottenham Hotspur to Real Madrid in 2013.

Barnett’s statement confirms that Doe filed a criminal complaint against him in London and that he is under investigation by London’s Metropolitan Police.

The Met previously stated that, last March, a 75-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of rape and causing grievous bodily harm when his flight landed at Heathrow Airport, before being released on bail.

A Met spokesperson told The Athletic: “Enquiries remain ongoing and there are no updates to provide at this current time.”

A key strand of Barnett’s response to Doe’s allegations is that he wants the complaint against him in the United States dismissed as he says he never met her in the country, and did not “knowingly or intentionally send her communications while she was in California”.

“I did not intentionally send Plaintiff any harassing text or other messages during any period of time when I was in California for business purposes, nor did I send Plaintiff any harassing text messages when I may have been vacationing in Florida.

“The allegations at paragraph 12 of Plaintiff’s declaration that I required Plaintiff to send me photos or videos of Plaintiff while I was located in California is false.”

Barnett also denied the suggestion that it “would not be difficult or burdensome for me to defend this action in California” as “absurd”.

“I am 76 years old, and suffer from a variety of health and physical conditions that make it difficult and uncomfortable for me to travel abroad regularly (from London) for short periods of time,” he said.

“Additionally, my psychological health has deteriorated significantly since Plaintiff made these allegations against me, and my family has suffered distress as a result of my situation, which allegations have been, and continue to be, the subject of widespread publicity.”

Barnett’s former employer, Creative Artists Agency (CAA), is also named in Doe’s U.S. lawsuit.

A CAA spokesperson told The Athletic last July: “While the complaint attempts to connect these allegations to CAA’s business, Ms. Doe has never been an employee, consultant, or contractor of CAA, ICM, or Stellar, nor has she ever had any business connection to CAA, ICM, or Stellar. Mr. Barnett exited Stellar in February 2024.”
